qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Proprietary WaveLogic coherent optical DSPs and integrated optical line systems create switching costs once deployed in carrier backbones. However, Ciena fails proof of moat: 10-year median ROIC is ~9.2%, with FY23-FY25 ROIC dropping to 3.3%-6.8%, well below the 12% hurdle. The company lacks pricing power >= inflation due to brutal oligopsonistic bargaining power from Tier-1 telcos and hyperscale cloud providers, combined with continuous 15-25% annual price-per-bit technological deflation. Key erosion threats include disaggregated open optical line systems and merchant coherent pluggables (800ZR/1600ZR).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, lack of pricing power >= inflation). Despite leading market share in coherent optical transmission and WaveLogic DSPs, Ciena sells into an oligopsony of hyperscalers (top cloud customer 17.8% of FY25 revenue) and Tier-1 telcos (AT&T 10.5%). The business faces structural 15-25% annual price-per-bit deflation and lumpy carrier capex cycles, resulting in a 10-year median ROIC of 9.2% and FY24-FY25 GAAP operating margins compressed to ~3%.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of ~9.2% fails the 12% cycle hurdle. In FY23, FY24, and FY25, ROIC stood at ~6.8%, ~3.4%, and ~4.2% respectively. GAAP operating margin compressed from 12.8% in FY21 to 2.99% in FY24 and 3.28% in FY25, while gross margin declined from 47.4% to 42.0%. Customer concentration is intense: a single unnamed hyperscale cloud provider contributed $851.6M (17.8% of FY25 revenue) and AT&T contributed $500.7M (10.5% of FY25 revenue). Sophisticated buyers wield immense RFP leverage against equipment vendors, forcing continuous heavy R&D reinvestment into next-generation DSPs just to offset hardware price deflation.
